summary: This bill prohibits the President from declaring a moratorium on hydraulic fracturing unless Congress passes a law authorizing it.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations. It solely addresses regulatory authority over hydraulic fracturing.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation does not address healthcare policy, insurance, or medical services in any way.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill is silent on immigration, border policy, or related enforcement.
No content concerning reproductive rights or abortion access.
No provisions affecting military budgets, defense policy, or armed forces.

The bill explicitly prohibits the President from declaring a moratorium on hydraulic fracturing without congressional approval and affirms state primacy over regulation. Hydraulic fracturing is an energy extraction technique frequently targeted by environmental regulations due to climate and ecological concerns. By blocking federal moratoriums, the legislation prevents a key form of environmental restriction and thereby limits environmental regulatory authority.
